Schema: OpenAPI **3.1.0** · API version **0.9.2** · 137 operations across 119 paths (124 require authentication).

Interactive documentation (`/docs`, `/redoc`) and the machine-readable schema (`/openapi.json`) are served **outside production only**; a production deployment disables all three (`main.create_app`).

## Operational notes

* `GET /health` — liveness only; a constant `{"status": "ok"}` payload with no version or environment disclosure.
* `GET /live` — process-alive probe (`{"status": "alive"}`).
* `GET /ready` — 200 only when the LLM provider is configured, the retrieval index is loaded and the database answers a trivial query; otherwise 503 with the failing dependency named. Provider name only (`{"status": "ready", "provider": "..."}`).
* `GET /metrics` — Prometheus exposition, omitted from this schema. In production it requires `METRICS_TOKEN` via `X-Metrics-Token` or a Bearer token; outside production it is open (`routers/system.py`).
* `GET /admin/system/info` — authenticated; the only endpoint that reports the app name, version and environment.
* Every response — including the 500 built by the unhandled-exception handler — carries `X-Request-ID` (the caller's value when it is a safe token, otherwise a generated one). CORS preflight responses are answered before the request-id middleware runs and are the one exception.
* When `must_change_password` is true (bootstrap admin), every route except `/health`, `/live`, `/ready`, `/metrics`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/change-password` and `/users/me` answers 403 until the password is rotated (`routers/deps.py`, `_FORCE_CHANGE_EXEMPT_PATHS`).

## Error contract

Three wire shapes, all of them declared in `routers/_error_contract.py`:

1. `{"detail": "<message>"}` — auth guards and single-message failures.
2. `{"detail": {"code": ..., "message": ..., <extras>}}` — business rules. `code` is a stable machine-readable string; switch on it, never on the message.
3. `{"detail": [{"loc": [...], "msg": ...}]}` — request/response validation (422), FastAPI's own shape.

## Rate limits

Applied per client IP unless the scope column says `user` (an authenticated caller's own budget, so one school NAT cannot lock out a classroom). Limits come from the running middleware configuration, including any `RATE_LIMIT_RULES` override; 429 responses carry `Retry-After`.

| Route prefix | Limit / window | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `/auth/forgot` | 10 / min | ip |
| `/auth/login` | 10 / min | ip |
| `/auth/mfa` | 20 / min | user |

## Configuration

Environment variables are documented in `.env.example` (generated from `Settings`, so every field the code reads appears there). Real `.env` files are never committed.
